summary.one_liner: data-to-paper is an automation framework in which interacting LLM and rule-based agents carry a research project from raw data through hypothesis, analysis, and writing to a complete, traceable scientific paper.
summary.what_it_does: The framework guides AI agents through an end-to-end research workflow: data exploration, literature search and ideation, statistical analysis code writing and debugging, result interpretation, and step-by-step paper writing. Its "data-chained" manuscripts link numeric values in the paper back to the code lines that produced them. It can run fully autonomously or be guided through a Copilot App, which supports inspecting the process, setting goals, requesting reviews, rewinding to earlier steps, recording and replaying runs, and tracking API costs. Standard statistical packages are wrapped with guardrails intended to reduce common LLM coding errors. The README says it is designed for relatively simple research goals and datasets where a statistical hypothesis is raised and tested. Built-in example datasets include diabetes (BRFSS), social network, NICU treatment policy, and pediatric intubation depth tasks.
use_cases: automatically generate a research paper from a dataset
trace numbers in a manuscript back to the code that produced them
test a statistical hypothesis on raw data with AI agents
compare machine learning and formula-based prediction methods
reproduce example research runs on bundled datasets
notable: Backward-traceable data-chained manuscripts linking numeric values to generating code lines
Autopilot or Copilot modes, with a Copilot App for human oversight and rewinding steps
Coding guardrails that override standard statistical packages to reduce LLM errors
Accompanies NEJM AI paper and arXiv preprint 2404.17605
caveats: Designed for relatively simple research goals and simple datasets, per the README
Not error-proof; the README says human intervention is necessary to ensure accuracy
Runs LLM-created code on the local machine and carries disclaimed risks
External LLM API token usage can be expensive; the user is responsible for monitoring costs
Installation dependencies are described in a separate INSTALL file, which was not included
